caption: The drawing features two main elements on a light beige background. On the left, there is a small rectangular grid diagram that uses blue and red lines on a pale base to represent a woven fabric pattern. The diagram is annotated with marks indicating “Alternate Repeat” horizontally and vertically, “Inches Each” at the top, and a scale at the bottom marked as ½” = 1’ 0”. The main object, located on the right, is a large weaving sample with a checkered pattern. The weave consists of intersecting stripes in blue, red, yellow, and white, forming a grid with alternating color blocks. The weaving has a fringe on three sides—the bottom, right, and upper right—with loose threads extending outward in blue, red, and yellow. The woven area is divided into alternating bands of tightly grouped colored sections and more open, grid-like sections, all created from horizontal and vertical stripes. A small label appears at the bottom right of the image, reading “RUTH BASSEL.”
title: Zoar Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
